## The transform

`unitTransformDist` builds distributions on the open interval (0,1) from
any base distribution on (0, Inf) via the odds-inverting transform
`Y = 1/(1+X)`. The base distribution is supplied directly as
density/CDF/quantile/random-generation functions -- there is no fixed
registry of allowed distributions.

```{r setup}
library(unitTransformDist)
set.seed(1)
```

```{r}
d <- utd(dgamma, pgamma, qgamma, rgamma, params = list(shape = 2.5))
dutd(0.3, d)
y <- rutd(500, d)
hist(y, breaks = 30, main = "Simulated (0,1)-valued data", xlab = "y")
```

## Fitting by maximum likelihood

```{r}
fit <- fit_utd_mle(y, dgamma, start = c(shape = 1), lower = c(shape = 1e-6))
fit
AIC(fit)
BIC(fit)
```

## The corrected profile-likelihood interval

A historical implementation mistake (carried over from an earlier
Python prototype of this idea) froze nuisance parameters at their
unconstrained MLE while profiling the parameter of interest. This
package's `profile_likelihood_ci()` re-optimizes nuisance parameters at
every candidate value instead, which is what the theory of profile
likelihood actually requires.

```{r}
ci <- profile_likelihood_ci(fit, "shape")
ci
```

## A fully custom, unregistered base distribution

Nothing above required `dgamma`/`pgamma` specifically. Any density and
CDF the user can write down works, including one with no closed-form
quantile function:

```{r}
dcustom <- function(x, rate, log = FALSE) dexp(x, rate = rate, log = log)
pcustom <- function(q, rate, lower.tail = TRUE) pexp(q, rate, lower.tail = lower.tail)
d2 <- utd(dcustom, pcustom, params = list(rate = 1.5), name = "custom_exp")
dutd(0.4, d2)
qutd(0.5, d2)  # obtained by numerically inverting pcustom, since qdist was not supplied
```

## Demonstrating the profile-likelihood fix empirically

`compare_profile_likelihood_coverage()` runs a small Monte Carlo study
comparing 95% coverage of the naive (broken) and corrected profile
likelihood on the same simulated data. This chunk is the package's
central empirical claim, and is fully reproducible by any user with the
seed fixed below.

```{r}
true_dist <- utd(dgamma, pgamma, qgamma, rgamma, params = list(shape = 2.5, rate = 1))
res <- compare_profile_likelihood_coverage(
  true_dist, c(shape = 2.5, rate = 1), dgamma,
  start = c(shape = 1, rate = 1), param_name = "shape",
  n = 60, n_sim = 150, lower = c(shape = 1e-6, rate = 1e-6), seed = 1)
res
```

## Bias correction

```{r}
bias_correct(fit, y, method = "jackknife")
```

## Monte Carlo study of estimator behaviour

```{r}
mc <- run_monte_carlo(d, true_params = c(shape = 2.5), ddist = dgamma,
                       start = c(shape = 1), lower = c(shape = 1e-6),
                       n = 100, n_sim = 200, seed = 1)
summary(mc)
```
